- Victims and sectors: Multiple organizations; sectors not disclosed by SOCRadar; Ukrainian and European targets mentioned in affiliate forum discussions
- Regions: Europe, Ukraine
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Unknown number of intrusions; SOCRadar tracking Oct 2026; affiliates share AI infrastructure and techniques across both RaaS families

Affiliates compromise target via RDP brute-force, stolen VPN credentials, or phishing; establish foothold with remote access

Install OpenCode framework with Claude 3.5 Opus or Kimi model; load 'network-recon', 'privilege-escalation', 'data-discovery' skills; agent begins autonomous operation

Agent scans Active Directory, identifies domain controllers, file servers, backups; maps network topology; generates PowerShell/C# privilege escalation payloads (Kimi assists with Chinese Windows environments); moves laterally

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/>

### exfil-ransomware: Data exfiltration and ransomware deployment (impact)

Agent stages sensitive data to Mega/SFTP; validates backup destruction; deploys INC Ransom or The Gentlemen ransomware; automated process reduces dwell time and increases success rate

# Cairn exposed panels / AIA0001–AIA0003

- ID: cairn-norforge-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-19
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cairn-norforge-2026-10/

## Summary
Operators run open-source Cairn harnesses that loop AI coding agents toward intrusion goals (unauthenticated RCE, uploader shells). Panels ship with no login and Compose binds 0.0.0.0:8000, so NorForge and scanners could read task text, tooling, and secrets. AI did not invent new exploits; it made patient web exploitation cheap (~10% success, ~23h to goal). Oct 26 update: NorForge discovered threat actors AIA0009/AIA0010 hijacking exposed Cairn panels themselves, harvesting SSH keys and operator secrets from compromised panels, deploying Poseidon RAT to take over panel infrastructure and pivot to operators' own systems.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
NorForge AIA0001 (Chinese language, CGI Global Limited / AS56594, high confidence), AIA0002 (English, Vultr/AS20473, high), AIA0003 (AlexHost, low). Financially motivated.

- Actor: NorForge AIA0001
- Actor ID: AIA0001
- Country: China
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: NorForge
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Unauthenticated web RCE / upload / deserialization / SQLi-to-RCE chains against e-commerce and payment sites (task-driven); CVE-2026-75650 Magento lab tooling observed on workers
- Victims and sectors: E-commerce / payment / merchant sites; AIA0001 mostly US, Japan, Australia; AIA0002 merchant/gray-market/pharma and some African commerce; Reuters-reported one operator into 100+ sites
- Regions: United States, Japan, Australia
- Region notes: Reported target geography includes the United States, Japan and Australia. Canada appeared in task text and African commerce was suggested by hints; those unconfirmed locations are excluded from country counts.
- Scale and metrics: 20+ malicious exposed panels; AIA0001 1,100+ projects across 14 panels; ~10% success; ~<$5/task estimate; <23h start-to-goal; TruffleHog hundreds of secrets (11% verified); Censys: 24 stock Cairn panel hosts

## Attack flow
### step-1: Operator assigns an intrusion goal (access)

Cairn workers receive tasks against web, commerce and payment sites.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### step-2: Coding agents plan and retry (ai)

The harness loops Claude Code or other agent backends toward the goal.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### step-3: Existing exploitation tools run (execution)

Workers attempt web RCE, upload and related exploitation chains.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### step-4: Some tasks obtain access (impact)

The research reports roughly 10% success; exposed harness panels also revealed operator tasks and secrets.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — The supplied source explicitly describes generative-model tooling assisting the reported activity; this mapping does not establish additional autonomy or victim impact.
  Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

## Prevention
Default-deny / GTFOBins-style block of nmap, python, php, openssl on web servers that do not need them; scan agent skills before load (LOLSkills); do not expose harness panels

## Detections
- Detect unexpected binaries on web servers (guidance) — Monitor execution of nmap, python, php, openssl, and other recon/development tools on web servers that typically serve HTTP/HTTPS only. Default-deny or application control policies are recommended.
- Detect agent harness panel exposure (guidance) — Scan for exposed Cairn or similar AI agent harness panels (default port 8000, no auth). Look for /api/*, /tasks, or panel-specific endpoints accessible without authentication.

# opencode remote MCP OAuth RCE

- ID: opencode-mcp-oauth-rce-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-19
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/opencode-mcp-oauth-rce-2026-10/

## Summary
Malicious or compromised remote MCP server returns 401 and OAuth discovery with attacker-controlled authorization_endpoint. opencode passes that URL to npm open; on Windows/WSL open 10.x builds a PowerShell -EncodedCommand without escaping the target, so $(...) in an https URL runs before the browser launches. No prompt injection required.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Vulnerability research (no in-the-wild campaign named)

- Actor: Vulnerability research (no in-the-wild campaign named)

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Developer connects coding agent to attacker-controlled or later-compromised remote MCP server
- Victims and sectors: Windows and WSL developers using opencode (~3M weekly npm downloads cited by Pillar)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Fixed in 1.18.33 (2026-09-28) without CVE/advisory; proposed CVSS 9.8

## Attack flow
### step-1: Developer connects a remote MCP server (access)

The server is attacker-controlled or later compromised.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### step-2: OAuth discovery supplies an attacker URL (ai)

A 401 response leads to an attacker-controlled authorization endpoint.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### step-3: URL enters PowerShell through open() (execution)

Affected Windows or WSL browser-opening code fails to escape the target.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### step-4: Commands execute before the browser opens (impact)

The injection occurs in the URL-opening path without requiring prompt injection.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
No ATLAS mapping is recorded.

## Prevention
Upgrade opencode; inventory installations (no CVE for scanners); pull unvetted remote MCP; argv not shell for URLs; MagicSword prevent unapproved second-stage binaries

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in opencode remote MCP OAuth RCE. Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) / [opencode-ai](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) 1.0.137–1.18.32
- MCP OAuth discovery

### Other tooling
- [npm open@10.1.2](https://github.com/sindresorhus/open)
- [PowerShell](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell)
- related class CVEs: CVE-2025-6514 [mcp-remote](https://github.com/punkpeye/mcp-remote), CVE-2025-58062 [openmcp-client](https://github.com/LSTM-Kirigaya/openmcp-client), CVE-2025-10619 [sequa-mcp](https://github.com/sequa-ai/sequa-mcp)

## Source notes
unknown

## Sources
- <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

# Wiz CIRT AI-driven multi-cloud intrusions

- ID: wiz-ai-driven-cloud-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-19
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/wiz-ai-driven-cloud-2026-10/

## Summary
AI agent ran full cloud operations: initial access, credential theft, pivots across GCP/AWS/K8s/CI-CD/IdP, debugging its own scripts. Loud (thousands of actions/hour), pentest-named resources, numeric task IDs with -b/-c retries, commented generated scripts. Lived off SSM, SA token minting, IdP admin creation, GitOps manifests, runner-log exfil.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Confirmed Java RCE in exposed Kafka UI among multiple probed doors; same source IP scanned 600+ other Wiz customer environments
- Victims and sectors: Large multi-cloud organization (Wiz customer); opportunistic scanning across many other customers
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Hundreds–thousands of actions per hour; 600+ environments scanned from same IP

## Attack flow
### step-1: Exposed Kafka UI is exploited (access)

The report confirms a Java RCE route among multiple probed entry points.

Evidence: <https://www.wiz.io/blog/anatomy-of-ai-driven-cloud-attacks>

### step-2: Agent executes and debugs cloud operations (ai)

The automation generates and retries scripts at high volume.

Evidence: <https://www.wiz.io/blog/anatomy-of-ai-driven-cloud-attacks>

### step-3: Credentials enable cross-service pivots (execution)

Reported paths span cloud accounts, Kubernetes, identity and CI/CD.

Evidence: <https://www.wiz.io/blog/anatomy-of-ai-driven-cloud-attacks>

### step-4: Data leaves through operational channels (impact)

The research describes runner-log exfiltration and abuse of legitimate cloud-management capabilities.

Evidence: <https://www.wiz.io/blog/anatomy-of-ai-driven-cloud-attacks>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS

  Evidence: <https://www.wiz.io/blog/anatomy-of-ai-driven-cloud-attacks>

## Prevention
Unify multi-platform logs; runtime visibility on runners/VMs/pods; restrict cross-system trust; rotate credentials on compromise; correlate loud agent tells (pentest- prefixes, task IDs)

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in Wiz CIRT AI-driven multi-cloud intrusions. Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

# Tensorlake AI sandbox SDK hijacked with Shai-Hulud stealer by ChainDrop

- ID: tensorlake-shai-hulud-chaindrop-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-17
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/tensorlake-shai-hulud-chaindrop-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 17, 2026: Actor 'ChainDrop' compromised Tensorlake maintainer's npm account via phishing. Published malicious TensorZero@1.8.4, @tensorzero/gateway@2.0.1, @tensorzero/cli@1.4.0. Embedded obfuscated Shai-Hulud infostealer targeting AI development credentials: Cursor IDE (.cursor/User/globalStorage/*.json), Claude Desktop (~/Library/Application Support/Claude), OpenAI keys (env vars, .openai/), GitHub tokens (~/.config/gh/), AWS credentials (~/.aws/), Docker configs, SSH keys. Exfiltrated to discord.com/api/webhooks/... and hxxps://tensorlakeapi[.]online/api/collect. Packages removed within 3 hours; ~450 downloads during window. TensorZero is LLM gateway/observability platform for engineering teams. ChainDrop previously linked to @tensorzero/keyv Mini Shai-Hulud campaign (Aug 7, GitGuardian) and other AI supply chain hits. Detection: monitor npm package.json for unexpected dependencies, review postinstall scripts, check for base64/eval obfuscation, scan for Discord webhook URLs, monitor file access to AI credential paths.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Actor 'ChainDrop'; linked to Mini Shai-Hulud keyv campaign (Aug 7); persistent targeting of AI development supply chains

- Actor: ChainDrop
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Socket Security
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: npm install of malicious @tensorzero/* packages (1.8.4, gateway@2.0.1, cli@1.4.0) via compromised maintainer account
- Victims and sectors: ~450 downloads during 3-hour window; AI/ML engineering teams using TensorZero; broader Shai-Hulud campaign targets AI developers
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: ~450 downloads in 3-hour window; packages removed within 3 hours of publication; part of broader Shai-Hulud campaign across AI tooling ecosystem

## Attack flow
### phish-maintainer: Compromise maintainer account (access)

ChainDrop phished Tensorlake maintainer's npm credentials to gain publish access to @tensorzero packages

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### publish-malicious: Publish malicious packages (ai)

Published malicious versions: TensorZero@1.8.4, @tensorzero/gateway@2.0.1, @tensorzero/cli@1.4.0 with embedded Shai-Hulud stealer in obfuscated postinstall script

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### execute-stealer: Execute credential harvesting (execution)

Postinstall script runs Shai-Hulud: scans filesystem for Cursor IDE config, Claude Desktop tokens, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, Docker configs, SSH keys; base64 encodes and stages

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### exfiltrate: Exfiltrate credentials (impact)

POST stolen credentials to Discord webhook and hxxps://tensorlakeapi[.]online/api/collect; credentials enable downstream AI service abuse and lateral movement

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### Connections

- phish-maintainer -> publish-malicious
- publish-malicious -> execute-stealer
- execute-stealer -> exfiltrate

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Supply chain compromise of AI development SDK to steal AI service credentials and API keys
  Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

## Prevention
Verify npm package integrity; review postinstall scripts; monitor for unexpected dependencies; use npm audit; implement software composition analysis (SCA); rotate credentials after suspected exposure; use credential vaults; monitor file access to AI credential stores; network egress filtering for Discord/unknown domains

## Detections
- npm postinstall script monitoring (guidance) — Monitor npm postinstall scripts for file system access to AI credential paths (~/.cursor/, ~/Library/Application Support/Claude, ~/.openai/, ~/.config/gh/, ~/.aws/); alert on Discord webhook URLs or unknown C2 domains in install scripts
- Network egress monitoring (guidance) — Alert on POST requests to tensorlakeapi\[.\]online or Discord webhook domains from npm/Node processes; monitor base64-encoded data exfiltration

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-17
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-10-17 (Socket Security): TensorZero packages compromised via phished maintainer credentials; ~450 downloads in 3-hour window before removal

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- TensorZero LLM gateway and observability platform
- [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/)
- [Claude Desktop](https://claude.com/product/overview)
- OpenAI API

### Other tooling
- Shai-Hulud credential stealer
- npm supply chain attack
- Discord webhooks for exfiltration
- tensorlakeapi\[.\]online C2

## Source notes
Socket Security analysis; TensorZero GitHub repo github.com/tensorlake/tensorzero. Related to s1ngularity-nx-ai-cli-2025-08 entry (Shai-Hulud targeting NX.dev AI CLI) and Mini Shai-Hulud keyv campaign. Detection: monitor for 'Shai-Hulud' patterns (Discord webhooks, base64 obfuscation in postinstall, AI credential path access .cursor/*, Claude config access, env var harvesting), alert on npm packages with obfuscated postinstall scripts, check for tensorlakeapi[.]online domain.

## Sources
- [Socket: AI Sandbox SDK Compromised in Supply Chain Attack](https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise)
- [TensorZero - LLM Gateway for Engineering Teams](https://github.com/tensorzero/tensorzero)

# Claude Agent SDK session-ID MCP RCE (CVE-2026-96620)

- ID: claude-agent-sdk-cve-2026-96620
- Reported: 2026-10-16
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/claude-agent-sdk-cve-2026-96620/

## Summary
SDK passed untrusted resume session ID to Claude CLI. IDs starting with '-' become CLI flags, enabling --mcp-config with a stdio MCP server that launches at startup outside SDK permission controls. CVSS 9.2.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Vulnerability (not a named campaign)

- Actor: Vulnerability (not a named campaign)

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Application must pass untrusted user-controlled session ID into resume
- Victims and sectors: Apps that let users pick/restore agent sessions
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Fixed in 0.2.121 on 2026-07-17; advisory public 2026-10-16

## Attack flow
### step-1: Application accepts a session ID (access)

An application passes an untrusted resume identifier into the SDK.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### step-2: Identifier becomes a CLI flag (execution)

A leading hyphen causes the supplied value to be interpreted as command-line options.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### step-3: MCP configuration is injected (ai)

The argument selects a stdio MCP server configuration.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### step-4: Server launches outside controls (impact)

The MCP startup command executes outside the SDK permission boundary.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0081](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0081) Modify AI Agent Configuration — Attacker-controlled CLI arguments inject an MCP startup configuration.
  Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

## Prevention
Upgrade SDK; validate CLI argv; treat attacker-touchable MCP config as code execution; app control on unexpected MCP-launched binaries

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in Claude Agent SDK session-ID MCP RCE (CVE-2026-96620). Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [claude-agent-sdk](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python) < 0.2.121
- [Claude CLI](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)
- stdio MCP

### Other tooling
- unknown

### MagicSword projects
- [LOLSkills](https://lolskills.io)

## Source notes
unknown

## Sources
- <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

# GhostAction Stage 2 stealer (AI credential theft)

- ID: ghostaction-ai-creds-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-16
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/ghostaction-ai-creds-2026-10/

## Summary
GhostAction pushes malicious GitHub Actions then Stage 2: .vscode/tasks.json folderOpen runs node on fake fa-solid-400.woff2 JS stealer; cron */5 pulls C2. Targets AWS/npm/git/kube/SSH plus Claude/Gemini creds. 94 repos / 66 owners. PolinRider copycat technique, not DPRK per OSM.

Evidence qualification: Primary attack is CI secret theft + VS Code folderOpen stealer; AI is a credential target (Claude/Gemini keys), not the attack operator. Included because Jose's post calls out AI tooling theft.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
GhostAction; PolinRider-technique copycat (no shared IOCs with DPRK per OSM)

- Actor: GhostAction

## AI involvement confidence
unverified

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Compromised GitHub account → malicious workflow + VS Code trusted workspace auto task
- Victims and sectors: GitHub maintainers / developers (many dormant repos)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 94 compromised repos; Stage 1 Oct 8, Stage 2 Oct 15 2026

## Attack flow
### step-1: Compromised account changes a repository (access)

Malicious GitHub Actions and workspace tasks are introduced.

Evidence: <https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/ghostaction-copycats-polinrider-by-hiding-a-stealer-in-a-fake-font-file>

### step-2: Trusted workspace opens a task (execution)

VS Code executes Node content disguised as a font file.

Evidence: <https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/ghostaction-copycats-polinrider-by-hiding-a-stealer-in-a-fake-font-file>

### step-3: AI credential stores are searched (ai)

The stealer targets Claude and Gemini tokens alongside cloud and developer credentials.

Evidence: <https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/ghostaction-copycats-polinrider-by-hiding-a-stealer-in-a-fake-font-file>

### step-4: Secrets are stolen with persistence (impact)

The report describes periodic C2 retrieval through cron and a multi-repository campaign.

Evidence: <https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/ghostaction-copycats-polinrider-by-hiding-a-stealer-in-a-fake-font-file>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0055](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0055) Unsecured Credentials — The stealer searches local AI credential stores.
  Evidence: <https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/ghostaction-copycats-polinrider-by-hiding-a-stealer-in-a-fake-font-file>

## Prevention
task.allowAutomaticTasks off; Restricted Mode; crontab -l for #ghc2; rotate Claude/Gemini/cloud/git creds

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in GhostAction Stage 2 stealer (AI credential theft). Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

# Aoki infostealer targets Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor tokens

- ID: symantec-aoki-infostealer-ai-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-15
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/symantec-aoki-infostealer-ai-2026-10/

## Summary
Aoki (aka Aokigahara) infostealer added AI credential theft in 2026. Targets: .claude.json, Claude desktop cookies, ChatGPT cookies, Codex config.toml/.env (github.com/openai/codex-cli), GitHub Copilot tokens (github.com/features/copilot), Cursor state.vscdb/storage.json (github.com/getcursor/cursor), Gemini CLI, JetBrains AI Assistant, Kiro, Windsurf, Codeium (github.com/Exafunction/codeium.vim), AWS credentials/SSO, Amazon Q, Git credentials, SSH keys. Cursor local state caches chat/code. Stolen keys allow acting under developer identity/quota, expose repos/cloud/CI-CD, bypass safeguards. Capable of LLMjacking. Earlier 2026 versions didn't target AI; capability recently added/expanding. Detection: monitor AI credential file access (.claude.json, .codex/auth.json, Cursor globalStorage), C2 domains (dobeqnesmot.cc, hjazfioe.surf), API usage anomalies from unexpected geolocations.

not assessed

- Victims and sectors: Developers using AI coding assistants; scale not disclosed
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Capability added 2026, expanding; no victim count

Aoki/Aokigahara deployed (distribution method not disclosed)

- ID: anyrun-fake-ai-tools-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-14
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/anyrun-fake-ai-tools-2026-10/

## Summary
1,258 public sandbox runs (Apr 15–Oct 5 2026) tied to lures as Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Ollama, OpenClaw, Manus. Patterns: InstallFix one-liner domain swap; ClickFix Download Claude via mshta; shared claude.ai/chatgpt.com chats; trojanized Claude_x64-setup.exe with mseupdate headless Edge cookie grab; BiTB fake AI ads for marketers.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution

# Visual Studio / SSMS Copilot trailing-dot RCE (CVE-2026-103572)

- ID: vs-copilot-trailing-dot-rce-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-13
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/vs-copilot-trailing-dot-rce-2026-10/

## Summary
Copilot edit guard blocked writes to .mcp.json via string compare. Writing '.mcp.json.' bypasses check; Win32 strips trailing dot so write lands on real MCP config → RCE via MCP server command or ripgrepPath pointing at arbitrary binary. Chainable via indirect prompt injection from a file or MCP server. Shared Microsoft.VisualStudio.Copilot.Core.dll affects VS 2022/2026 and SSMS. Patched with GetFullPath.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Vulnerability research; CVE-2026-103572 CVSS 8.8 Important

- Actor: Vulnerability research

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Indirect prompt injection (file content / MCP) into Copilot chat, or misaligned agent
- Victims and sectors: Visual Studio and SSMS users
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Patched 2026-10-13 Patch Tuesday

## Attack flow
### step-1: Untrusted instructions reach Copilot (access)

A file or MCP server supplies indirect instructions.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### step-2: Agent edits a protected configuration name (ai)

Writing .mcp.json. bypasses a string-based edit check.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### step-3: Windows normalizes the trailing dot (execution)

The write reaches the real MCP configuration or executable-path setting.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### step-4: Attacker-chosen command runs (impact)

The changed MCP startup command or binary path enables code execution.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

  Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>
- [AML.T0081](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0081) Modify AI Agent Configuration — The resulting edit modifies MCP startup or executable configuration.
  Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

# Langflow MCP-config RCE (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2, GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45)

- ID: langflow-mcp-rce-ghsa-2026
- Reported: 2026-10-11
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/langflow-mcp-rce-ghsa-2026/

## Summary
GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2 (CVE-2026-105697) and GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45: Authenticated Langflow users can achieve RCE by adding MCP server with Stdio transport. User-supplied command field passed directly to bash -c 'exec {command}' with zero validation, no allowlisting, no sandboxing. Env field allows arbitrary environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, PATH override). Command executes when server list fetched with action_count=true - happens automatically in UI MCP settings page. Affects <1.9.0 (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2) and <1.10.3 (GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45). Default LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true hands out token without credentials. Previdian honeypots recorded 1,423 exploitation attempts from 27 IPs (Belgium, China, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Nigeria, Philippines, Russia, Seychelles, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Tanzania, US, Vietnam) beginning Sep 19, 2026. Attackers first checked auto-login, then brute-forced credentials. Fixed in 1.9.0 (command allowlist) and 1.10.3 (full policy enforcement, removed bash wrapper). GitHub: github.com/langflow-ai/langflow.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Multiple attackers from 27 countries; financially motivated/opportunistic exploitation

- Actor: Multiple opportunistic attackers
- Country: Multiple (27 countries)
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Previdian, VulnCheck
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Authenticated user access (or LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true provides token without credentials); exploitation via POST/PATCH /api/v2/mcp/servers/{server_name} or embedded flow configs
- Victims and sectors: Langflow installations; multiple internet-facing vulnerable instances found; 1,423 exploitation attempts against Previdian honeypots from 27 countries
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 1,423 exploitation attempts against Previdian honeypots from 27 IPs (Sep 19-Oct 2026); 333 attempts on Oct 11 alone; first attempts Sep 19 (2+ weeks before CVE publication Oct 5); dramatic increase post-CVE

## Attack flow
### auth: Obtain authentication (access)

Default LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true provides token without credentials via GET /api/v1/auto_login; or brute-force credentials if auto-login disabled

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45>

### inject-command: Add malicious MCP server (ai)

POST/PATCH /api/v2/mcp/servers/{server_name} with Stdio transport; command field contains arbitrary OS command (reverse shell, file operations, etc.); env field can inject LD_PRELOAD, PATH override

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

### trigger: Trigger execution (execution)

Command executes automatically when GET /api/v2/mcp/servers?action_count=true (happens when anyone navigates to MCP settings page); re-executes every time list loaded; persistent backdoor

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

### rce: Remote code execution (impact)

User-supplied command wrapped in bash -c 'exec {command}' and executed; no validation, allowlisting, or sandboxing; runs with Langflow process privileges; full server compromise possible

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

### Connections

- auth -> inject-command
- inject-command -> trigger
- trigger -> rce

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Exploitation of vulnerability in AI workflow platform (Langflow) via MCP server misconfiguration
  Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

## Prevention
Upgrade to Langflow 1.10.3+; disable LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN; enforce strong unique passwords; review MCP server configurations; monitor /api/v2/mcp/servers/ API access; check for unexpected command/env entries; network segmentation; principle of least privilege

## Detections
- Monitor MCP server API endpoints (guidance) — Monitor POST/PATCH requests to /api/v2/mcp/servers/ endpoints for suspicious command parameters; alert on bash -c execution patterns, environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, PATH overrides), and auto-login token generation from unexpected IPs
- File system monitoring (guidance) — Monitor Langflow process for execution of child processes via bash; alert on unexpected shell command execution from Langflow worker processes

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-09-19
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-09-19 (Previdian honeypots): First exploitation attempts observed, 2+ weeks before CVE publication
- 2026-10-05 (GitHub Security Advisory): CVE published
- 2026-10-11 (Previdian, The Hacker News): 333 exploitation attempts on this day alone; public disclosure

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Langflow AI workflow platform
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) Stdio transport

### Other tooling
- bash command execution
- Environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONPATH, BASH_ENV)

## Source notes
Two GitHub Security Advisories (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2 for <1.9.0, GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45 for <1.10.3); Previdian observed exploitation 2+ weeks before public CVE; VulnCheck analysis of AI stack vulnerabilities. Detection: monitor Langflow API /api/v2/mcp/servers/ for suspicious commands, review MCP Stdio configs, check for bash -c execution, monitor env var injection patterns (LD_PRELOAD, PATH), alert on auto-login token requests from unexpected IPs.

## Sources
- [GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2: Authenticated RCE via MCP Stdio transport](https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2)
- [GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45: OS command injection RCE via MCP stdio](https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45)

# Adception fake Claude Mac InstallFix

# C2Agent LLM-driven Windows implant

- ID: c2agent-unit42-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-09
- AI role: ai_infra_as_c2
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/c2agent-unit42-2026-10/

## Summary
Go Windows implant where an LLM on the C2 side drives the host: operator sends a plain-language goal; implant builds a system prompt (tools, MCP, skills, memory), model returns one JSON tool call, agent executes and feeds TOOL RESULT back, loop until done (default 40 steps). Built-in MCP client defaults to Firecrawl public MCP; C2 can add MCP servers and markdown skill playbooks; skill_save lets the LLM propose new skills. From v2.3 can hand tasks to AI coding CLIs already on the host; v2.4 adds Cobalt Strike BOF loader and self-upgrade.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
unknown; 32 samples ~1 month active development

- Actor: unknown

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: unknown (two-stage: Go stager downloads PE from agent.x90.dev/data/copilot.txt)
- Victims and sectors: unknown (no victim orgs named in Unit 42 timely intel note)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 32 samples 2026-09-10 to 2026-10-08 (25 agents, 8 major versions in 29 days; 7 stager v7); payload URL live serving v2.4 as of 2026-10-09

# AgentCorruption (AWS Bedrock AgentCore IMDS)

- Reported: 2026-10-08

## Summary

Default role was region-wide across AgentCore: invoke other agents, read conversations/memories, pull images, Secrets Manager / AgentCore Identity, plant persistent memory hijacks. AWS tightened IMDSv2 defaults and narrowed default role.

# ARTEX + Claude Code vs South Korean finance

- ID: crowdstrike-artex-sk-finance-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-07
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/crowdstrike-artex-sk-finance-2026-10/

## Summary
Likely Chinese-speaking financially motivated actor used open-source Chinese agentic pentest suite ARTEX plus Claude Code against South Korean financial orgs. Open directories held Claude session histories, ARTEX configs, Claude memory. ARTEX used DeepSeek v4.1-flash via xcai.pro; also GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6. Actor asked Claude where to sell Korean breach data. ARTEX later went closed-source.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
CrowdStrike did not attribute the activity to a named adversary. It assessed with moderate confidence that the actor was likely a Chinese speaker and financially motivated.

- Actor: Unknown threat actor
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: CrowdStrike Intelligence
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting

- Victims and sectors: South Korean financial organizations (multiple banks per industry reports)
- Regions: South Korea
- Region notes: South Korea describes victim financial organizations. Chinese language concerns actor attribution; Hong Kong refers to infrastructure. Neither is counted as victim geography.
- Scale and metrics: Active late September through early October 2026. The number of organizations was not confirmed in the 7 October CrowdStrike report. FBI FLASH-20261113-001 says this South Korean financial campaign exfiltrated personal information of approximately 67,000 individuals, citing CrowdStrike, Zscaler, and CERT-EU.

# PoeLLM botnet targets 3,400+ exposed LiteLLM/Ollama servers for mining

- ID: lumen-poellm-botnet-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-07
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/lumen-poellm-botnet-2026-10/

## Summary
PoeLLM malware exploits vulnerable internet-facing AI/LLM deployments (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520). Derives C2 from keywords in poem 'On the Nature of Connection' hosted in GitHub repo ejejejdfbbebe/nodejs.org fork (dash.css file). Malware parses poem to extract 4 words/phrases via pattern matching ('In the silent hum of X,', 'each pulse of X threading', 'Beyond the wall of X,', 'the X servers'), converts words to numbers via hardcoded dictionary, combines to form IPv4 C2 address. Deploys XMRig and Iron crypto miners connecting to Kryptex (5.180.174.162). Converts victims into HTTP/S scanners and exploit servers for expansion. Poem updated 11 times since Apr 13, 2026 to rotate C2. Italian-speaking actor. 3,400+ victims, peak 800 active/day, predominantly US/Western Europe.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Canto Incognito campaign; Italian-speaking threat actor (assessment); financially motivated cryptocurrency mining operation

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Exploitation of publicly exposed vulnerable services: LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520; first activity April 2026
- Victims and sectors: 3,400+ victim servers; enterprise AI infrastructure; development toolkits; predominantly US and Western Europe; peak activity 800 active servers per day
- Regions: United States, Europe
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Active since April 2026; 3,400+ impacted servers; peak ~2,200 affected servers mid-June, ~800 active per day; first C2 commit Apr 13, 2026; poem updated 11 times; broader scanning/exploitation began May 2026; recent traffic suggests distributed brute-force experiments

## Attack flow
### vuln-exploit: Exploit vulnerable AI/LLM services (access)

Target publicly exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520; Gotenberg docs explicitly warn not to expose to internet

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### poem-c2: GitHub poem-derived C2 (execution)

Malware queries GitHub repo ejejejdfbbebe/nodejs.org fork for dash.css; parses poem 'On the Nature of Connection' to extract 4 words ('In the silent hum of X', 'each pulse of X threading', 'Beyond the wall of X', 'the X servers'); converts words to numbers via hardcoded dictionary; combines to IPv4 C2 address; poem updated 11 times since Apr 13, 2026

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### deploy-malware: Deploy libgcrypt malware (execution)

Downloads and executes ELF 'libgcrypt' from C2; malware includes remote shell, XMRig and Iron crypto miners, HTTP/S scanning capabilities, exploit deployment

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### mining: Cryptocurrency mining (ai)

Deploys XMRig and Iron miners; connects to Kryptex mining service at 5.180.174.162; GPU hardware attractive target for mining

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### expand-botnet: Convert victims to scanners (impact)

Infected servers become HTTP/S vulnerability scanners and exploit servers; proxy attacks through compromised hosts to expand botnet; repurposed routers for C2 infrastructure; recent experiments with distributed brute-force

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### Connections

- vuln-exploit -> poem-c2
- poem-c2 -> deploy-malware
- deploy-malware -> mining
- deploy-malware -> expand-botnet
- expand-botnet -> vuln-exploit [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010) AI Supply Chain Compromise — Supply chain-style targeting of exposed AI/LLM services (LiteLLM, Ollama) for compromise and cryptocurrency mining
  Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Exploitation of vulnerabilities in AI/LLM infrastructure (possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520, vulnerable LiteLLM/Ollama versions)
  Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

Do not expose AI/LLM services to internet (Gotenberg guidance explicit); vulnerability patching for LiteLLM/Ollama/Gitea/Ivanti Sentry; monitor for crypto mining (Kryptex 5.180.174.162); GitHub repository monitoring; C2 poem pattern detection; HTTP scanning from AI servers; GPU utilization anomalies

No detections are recorded.

- [Ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama)

# CyberXero IAB deploys up to 51 Claude Code agents against Ukrainian energy

- ID: cyberxero-iab-ukraine-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-06
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cyberxero-iab-ukraine-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 6, 2026: SOCRadar tracked CyberXero (initial access broker) targeting Ukrainian energy companies with large-scale AI agent deployment. Initial access via spearphishing and exploitation of public-facing Fortinet VPN (CVE-2024-47575). Post-compromise: (1) Deploy up to 51 parallel Claude Code agents across compromised hosts; (2) Each agent assigned role: 'recon', 'privilege-escalation', 'lateral-movement', 'persistence', 'data-discovery'; (3) Agents collaborate: share findings via shared SQLite database on C2; coordinate to avoid duplicate work; (4) Agents generate exploits for internal vulnerabilities (SMB, RDP, unpatched Windows servers); (5) Target SCADA/ICS systems, OT networks, backup infrastructure; (6) After mapping and access escalation, CyberXero sells access to highest bidder (ransomware groups, nation-state actors, wipers). SOCRadar observed 7 compromised Ukrainian energy companies Sep-Oct 2026. Median time from initial access to full domain compromise: 18 hours (compared to 72+ hours for manual operators). Detection: monitor for multiple Claude API-calling processes from single host or network; detect agent coordination patterns (shared database writes); alert on rapid privilege escalation across multiple hosts; review exploit payloads for LLM generation patterns; monitor SCADA/ICS network access from IT networks.

## Category
uncategorized

- Scale and metrics: 7 Ukrainian energy companies compromised; up to 51 parallel AI agents per target; median 18 hours from initial access to domain compromise (vs 72+ hours manual)

# CLOSEDQUORUM implant - 4 LLMs vote on next action

- ID: talos-closedquorum-implant-2026-09
- Reported: 2026-09-22
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/talos-closedquorum-implant-2026-09/

## Summary
CLOSEDQUORUM is a Go-based Windows implant that queries DeepSeek, Qwen (via OpenRouter), Mistral, and Gemini in sequence for post-compromise decisions. Each model receives system info (hostname, Windows version, admin status) and a constrained JSON prompt with 4 actions: steal (credentials/browsers/wallets), inject (process hollowing), persist (registry/startup), or move (no handler in the public build). Models vote; plurality wins; ties favor DeepSeek > Qwen > Mistral > Gemini. Decisions are posted to a Discord webhook with reasoning. No human operator commands are needed after deployment. The public build uses dummy keys and a dummy webhook, so Talos did not observe end-to-end execution. Talos discovered it via CAIRN, its open-source AI-malware hunting toolkit. Developer artifacts link to carding forums dating to 2025.

Evidence qualification: Public distribution build contains dummy API keys and webhook; Talos has not observed end-to-end run or confirmed in-the-wild deployment; binary artifacts connect developer to carding forum postings dating to 2025

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Developer artifacts link to carding forum postings dating to 2025; no confirmed threat actor attribution

- Actor: Unknown
- Motivation: unknown
- Attributed by: Cisco Talos
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Not established in public sample; deployment method unknown
- Victims and sectors: No confirmed in-the-wild deployment; public sample analysis only
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: First publicly documented autonomous AI C2 implant; analysis dated Jun 17, 2026; disclosed Sep 22, 2026; public build non-functional (dummy keys)

## Attack flow
### deployment: Implant deployment (access)

Go-based Windows implant deployed (method unknown in public sample); no confirmed in-the-wild deployment

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### system-enum: System enumeration (execution)

Collects hostname, Windows version, administrator status for LLM query context

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### llm-vote: LLM panel voting (ai)

Queries 4 LLM providers in sequence: DeepSeek, Qwen (OpenRouter), Mistral, Gemini; sends system info and constrained JSON prompt with 4 actions (steal, inject, persist, move); each model votes; plurality wins; ties favor DeepSeek > Qwen > Mistral > Gemini; no quorum threshold

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### discord-log: Decision logging to Discord (execution)

Posts winning decision and model's stated reasoning to Discord webhook before execution; stolen data also sent to same webhook

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### execute: Execute decision (impact)

Executes winning action: steal (credentials, browsers, wallets), inject (process hollowing via CreateProcessW CREATE_SUSPENDED), persist (registry/startup), or move (no handler); public build injection reaches primitives but demonstrates no successful execution

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### Connections

- deployment -> system-enum
- system-enum -> llm-vote
- llm-vote -> discord-log
- discord-log -> execute
- execute -> system-enum [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — First documented Windows implant using LLM panel voting for autonomous C2 decisions; represents shift where expanding portions of attack chain execute without operator involvement
  Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

## Prevention
AI API key monitoring; Discord webhook traffic from unexpected processes; plurality voting pattern detection; LLM query patterns with system enumeration; CAIRN tool for AI-malware hunting

## Detections
- Correlated LLM-provider and Discord traffic (guidance) — Alert on unexpected Windows processes contacting several LLM providers and Discord webhooks within the same execution window.
- Autonomous implant behavior correlation (guidance) — Correlate LLM API traffic with LSASS access, process injection, persistence creation, or repeated execution at randomized intervals.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-06-17
- Last updated: 2026-09-22
- 2026-09-22 (Cisco Talos): Talos published its static analysis and stated that it had no confirmation of in-the-wild deployment.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [DeepSeek](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (api.deepseek.com, deepseek-chat)
- Qwen (via OpenRouter, qwen/qwen-2.5-72b-instruct)
- Mistral (api.mistral.ai, mistral-large-latest)
- Google [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) (gemini-2.0-flash-exp)

### Other tooling
- Discord webhook for decision logging and exfiltration
- [CAIRN](https://github.com/oritera/Cairn) (Talos AI-malware hunting tool, used for discovery)
- Go-based implant
- Windows process injection primitives (CreateProcessW, CREATE_SUSPENDED)

## Source notes
Cisco Talos first public documentation; discovered via CAIRN. Talos reports that the public distribution binary is inert because it contains dummy API keys and a dummy webhook. Static analysis confirms plurality voting and deterministic tie-breaking, not a minimum 3-of-4 quorum; if every provider fails, an unhandled consensus value causes the loop to sleep and retry.

## Sources
- [The Closed Quorum: Inside the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/)

# ChatGPT Lockdown Mode bypass - HTML preview sandbox escape (Check Point)

- ID: chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-checkpoint-2026-09
- Reported: 2026-09-18
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-checkpoint-2026-09/

## Summary
Check Point researcher Alexey Bukhteyev disclosed ChatGPT Lockdown Mode bypass allowing HTML preview sandbox escape via contentWindow.open from nested iframe. Attack vectors: (1) zero-click desktop chat history theft, (2) fake-update malware delivery pages, (3) credential phishing via malicious prompts, custom GPTs, or shared chat links. OpenAI patched vulnerability Sept 18, 2026. No evidence of in-the-wild exploitation; marked borderline as researcher disclosure only.

Evidence qualification: Researcher disclosure; OpenAI fixed Sept 18, 2026; no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Researcher disclosure (Alexey Bukhteyev, Check Point); no threat actor; OpenAI patched Sept 18

- Actor: Researcher disclosure only
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: unknown
- Attributed by: Check Point
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Malicious prompt, custom GPT, or shared chat link with HTML preview exploit
- Victims and sectors: ChatGPT users; theoretical risk only (fixed before in-wild use)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: PoC only; patched Sept 18, 2026; no in-wild exploitation documented

## Attack flow
### craft-exploit: Craft HTML preview exploit (execution)

Attacker creates malicious prompt/GPT/shared chat with nested iframe contentWindow.open escape

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### deliver-link: Deliver via prompt/GPT/shared chat (access)

User interacts with malicious prompt, custom GPT, or shared chat link

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### escape-sandbox: Escape HTML preview sandbox (execution)

Nested iframe contentWindow.open escapes Lockdown Mode sandbox

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### exfil-or-phish: Chat history theft or credential phishing (impact)

Zero-click chat history exfiltration (desktop) or credential phishing popup

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### Connections

- craft-exploit -> deliver-link
- deliver-link -> escape-sandbox
- escape-sandbox -> exfil-or-phish

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051) LLM Prompt Injection — Malicious prompts/GPTs/shared chats could deliver HTML preview exploits
  Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>
- [AML.T0077](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0077) LLM Response Rendering — Sandbox escape enabled chat history theft (zero-click desktop)
  Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>
- [AML.T0057](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0057) LLM Data Leakage — Credential phishing via escaped sandbox popup windows
  Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

## Prevention
OpenAI patched Sept 18, 2026; users should update ChatGPT Desktop; avoid untrusted shared chat links; review custom GPT permissions; implement sandbox escape monitoring

## Detections
- ChatGPT security monitoring (guidance) — Update ChatGPT Desktop to post-Sept-18-2026 version; monitor for sandbox escape attempts; review shared chat links before opening; audit custom GPT permissions; implement popup blocker; detect contentWindow.open from nested iframes; educate users on malicious prompt/GPT risks

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-09-18
- Last updated: 2026-09-18

# ESET GuardBreaker - UAC-0099 plants a refusal-bait comment in a MATCHBOIL script

- ID: eset-guardbreaker-uac-0099-decoy-prompt-2026-08
- Reported: 2026-08-27
- AI role: other
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/eset-guardbreaker-uac-0099-decoy-prompt-2026-08/

## Summary
ESET Research described GuardBreaker in posts on X on Aug 27, 2026. Tomáš Foltýn's WeLiveSecurity article followed on Sep 10, 2026. In a VBScript used early in an attack on a target in Ukraine, UAC-0099 left inert REM comments. Help Net Security quotes the opening as a request to make a nuclear weapon and to help, followed by uranium-enrichment text. The comment has no runtime effect. ESET says it is there so an LLM-powered code scanner's safety guardrails refuse the file and stop reading before the payload logic. ESET names this a reverse jailbreak: the point is to cause a refusal, not to talk a model into complying. The script's job is to download and install MATCHBOIL, a loader ESET says is used only by UAC-0099. The same group has checked for IDA and Wireshark processes in other attacks. ESET did not test whether the comment works and did not name a targeted model. DugganUSA, in an independent write-up dated Sep 1, 2026, ran one A/B pass on a synthetic inert script: GPT-4o and Mistral analyzed the treatment and flagged the decoy, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 returned an empty refusal. That test is not ESET's, and DugganUSA says it is a single sample on one day. UAC-0099 is Russia-aligned, active since at least 2022, and has targeted Ukrainian transportation and energy. Reporting says the group has handed validated access to Sandworm. On Jul 21, 2026 CERT-UA documented an updated chain: a VBS script with a fake extension and a long run of spaces before .vbs, Notepad++ 8.8.3 components, and the tools LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, and MATCHBOIL.V2. That advisory is about the group and the loader, not about the GuardBreaker comment. ATT&CK does not have a technique for a refusal bait in a comment. The script execution itself is T1059.005.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
UAC-0099, Russia-aligned, espionage. ESET attributes the script and the GuardBreaker comment. CERT-UA attributes the group's MATCHBOIL, LUNCHPOKE, and BURNYBEAR tooling. ESET does not claim this sample was handed to Sandworm.

- Actor: UAC-0099
- Country: Russia
- Motivation: nation-state
- Attributed by: ESET Research; CERT-UA for the group and its loaders
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
vendor-asserted

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: A VBScript used in the early stage of an intrusion at a Ukrainian organization. ESET does not describe how the script arrived. CERT-UA's July chain for the same group starts from a phishing ZIP that contains a VBS file disguised with a fake extension.
- Victims and sectors: An unnamed organization in Ukraine. UAC-0099's usual targets include transportation and energy.
- Regions: Ukraine
- Region notes: Ukraine is the victim location ESET gives for this script. Russia is the actor alignment, not a victim region.
- Scale and metrics: One documented script in one early-stage intrusion. ESET did not report how often the comment has been used or whether a scanner refused this sample.

## Attack flow
### vbs-stage: VBScript in an early stage (access)

UAC-0099 uses a VBScript early in an intrusion against a target in Ukraine. The script's runtime job is to download and install MATCHBOIL.

Evidence: <https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/business-security/guardbreaker-derailing-ai-assisted-malware-analysis-code-comment/>

### decoy-comment: Inert refusal-bait comment (ai)

REM comments request help with a nuclear weapon and then add enrichment text. They do not execute. ESET says they are meant to make an LLM scanner refuse before it reaches the loader logic.

Evidence: <https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/business-security/guardbreaker-derailing-ai-assisted-malware-analysis-code-comment/> <https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/31/russian-hackers-ai-safety-filters-manipulation/>

### loader: MATCHBOIL still installs (execution)

If the script is run, it still downloads MATCHBOIL, the group's loader. CERT-UA's July chain uses a double-extension VBS, Notepad++ components, LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, and MATCHBOIL.V2.

Evidence: <https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/business-security/guardbreaker-derailing-ai-assisted-malware-analysis-code-comment/> <https://cert.gov.ua/article/6318634>

### scanner-gap: A refusal is the gap (impact)

ESET did not measure the effect. DugganUSA's separate one-day test saw one of three models return an empty refusal and the other two flag the decoy and continue.

Evidence: <https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/business-security/guardbreaker-derailing-ai-assisted-malware-analysis-code-comment/> <https://www.dugganusa.com/post/we-tested-the-russian-anti-analysis-trick-on-three-models-two-analyzed-the-sample-and-flagged-the-d>

### Connections

- vbs-stage -> decoy-comment
- vbs-stage -> loader
- decoy-comment -> scanner-gap

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.001) Indirect — The refusal bait is indirect prompt injection: untrusted text inside a file being analyzed is meant to reach the model and cut the analysis short.
  Evidence: <https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/business-security/guardbreaker-derailing-ai-assisted-malware-analysis-code-comment/>
- [AML.T0015](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0015) Evade AI Model — The intended effect is evasion of an AI model used as a code scanner, by provoking a safety refusal before the payload logic is read.
  Evidence: <https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/business-security/guardbreaker-derailing-ai-assisted-malware-analysis-code-comment/>

## Prevention
Keep the scanner's instructions separate from the file under analysis, and treat text inside the sample as data. A refusal, an empty completion, or a safety block on a malware sample should raise a review, not end it. Fall back to analysis that does not depend on a model, and do not give one model the only vote on whether a file is safe. The comment does not change what the script does when Windows runs it, so script-host and loader detections still apply.

## Detections
- [Cscript/Wscript Uncommon Script Extension Execution](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_wscript_cscript_uncommon_extension_exec.yml) (sigma) — Selected from a security-detections-mcp search for wscript. Windows process creation. wscript.exe or cscript.exe whose command line contains a non-script extension such as .pdf, .doc, or .txt. CERT-UA described UAC-0099 VBS names with a fake document extension, spaces, and then .vbs. A command line that still contains .pdf matches. A plain .vbs path with no fake extension does not.
- [Suspicious Double Extension Files](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/file/file_event/file_event_win_susp_double_extension.yml) (sigma) — Selected from a security-detections-mcp search for double extension. Windows file event. A created file whose name ends in a document extension immediately followed by .vbs, .exe, or another listed payload extension, including .pdf.vbs. The spaced form described by CERT-UA, with characters between pdf and .vbs, does not match this regex.
- [Vbscript Execution Using Wscript App](https://github.com/splunk/security_content/blob/develop/detections/endpoint/vbscript_execution_using_wscript_app.yml) (splunk) — Selected from a security-detections-mcp search for VBScript. Endpoint process data for wscript.exe executing VBScript. This is the generic script-host path for the GuardBreaker file. It does not know that the comment is a refusal bait.
- Refusal-bait comments and MATCHBOIL (guidance) — security-detections-mcp searches for VBScript, wscript, and double extension did not return a rule that looks for refusal-bait wording or for MATCHBOIL. A YARA or Sigma hunt for inert comments that request help building a weapon, sitting above a downloader, is still a written hunt rather than a published rule. Do not treat a scanner refusal as a benign verdict. CERT-UA's July chain also drops Notepad++ components and LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, and MATCHBOIL.V2; those names are not in the indexed rules.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-08-27
- Last updated: 2026-09-10
- 2026-07-21 (CERT-UA): CERT-UA documents UAC-0099's updated chain, including a double-extension VBS, Notepad++ 8.8.3 components, LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, and MATCHBOIL.V2. The advisory does not describe the refusal-bait comment.
- 2026-08-27 (ESET Research): ESET posts the GuardBreaker finding on X: a UAC-0099 VBScript used early against a target in Ukraine carries an inert comment meant to make an LLM code scanner refuse.
- 2026-08-31 (Help Net Security): Help Net Security recounts the X posts, the nuclear-weapon comment, and the MATCHBOIL downloader.
- 2026-09-01 (DugganUSA): Independent A/B test on a synthetic script. One of three models returned an empty refusal. The other two analyzed the sample and flagged the decoy. DugganUSA says this is not a benchmark.
- 2026-09-10 (WeLiveSecurity): Tomáš Foltýn publishes the GuardBreaker article. ESET still does not report a test of the comment or name a targeted model.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Unnamed LLM-powered code scanner. ESET did not name a model.
- DugganUSA's independent test used [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o, and Mistral. That test is not the incident.

### Other tooling
- MATCHBOIL loader, delivered by the script
- Windows Script Host (wscript.exe or cscript.exe)

## Source notes
The comment's role, the MATCHBOIL purpose, the Ukraine victim, and the IDA and Wireshark checks are from the WeLiveSecurity article (Sep 10, 2026) and the Aug 31 Help Net Security recap of the X posts. The enrichment procedure is not repeated here. DugganUSA is independent research on a synthetic sample; it is not a test of the incident file. CERT-UA article 6318634 (Jul 21, 2026) is the government write-up of the group's VBS, Notepad++, LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, and MATCHBOIL.V2 chain. https://cybernews.com/security/russian-hackers-nuclear-prompt-ai-guardrails/ returned HTTP 403 during link checks and is omitted. No YARA or Sigma rule in the detection index matches the refusal-bait wording or the name MATCHBOIL.

# UAT-10147 uses PentestGPT and AI scripts in SEO-fraud intrusions

- ID: uat-10147-pentestgpt-seo-fraud-2026-08
- Reported: 2026-08-20
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/uat-10147-pentestgpt-seo-fraud-2026-08/

## Summary
Aug 20, 2026: Cisco Talos tracked UAT-10147 (Chinese-speaking, financially motivated) conducting SEO-fraud intrusions against e-commerce, media, hospitality websites. Initial access via WordPress/Drupal/Joomla CMS exploits and credential stuffing. Post-compromise: (1) Deploy PentestGPT (open-source penetration testing framework using GPT-4/Claude for autonomous security testing); (2) Run custom AI scripts (Python + LLM API calls) to identify additional vulnerabilities, enumerate databases, discover admin panels; (3) Inject SEO spam (backlinks to gambling, pharma, counterfeit goods sites) into database; (4) Install webshells for persistence; (5) Monetize via click fraud and affiliate schemes. Talos observed UAT-10147 in 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026. PentestGPT automates privilege escalation and lateral movement. AI scripts generate SQL injection payloads adapting to WAF rules. Detection: monitor for PentestGPT indicators (Python process with GPT-4/Claude API calls, pentestgpt command-line tool); detect AI-generated SQL injection patterns; alert on SEO spam injection into CMS databases; review webshell deployments; check for unexpected LLM API traffic from web servers.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
UAT-10147 (Chinese-speaking actor); financially motivated (SEO fraud, click fraud, affiliate schemes); Talos tracking cluster

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: WordPress, Drupal, Joomla CMS vulnerability exploitation; credential stuffing attacks
- Victims and sectors: 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026; e-commerce, media, hospitality websites; small to medium businesses
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026; AI automation enables high-volume SEO-fraud operations

## Attack flow
### cms-exploitation: Exploit CMS vulnerabilities (access)

UAT-10147 compromises WordPress, Drupal, Joomla sites via known CVEs or credential stuffing; gains webserver access

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### deploy-ai-tools: Deploy PentestGPT and AI scripts (ai)

Install PentestGPT (open-source pentest framework using GPT-4/Claude); run custom Python AI scripts for vulnerability discovery, database enumeration, admin panel discovery

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### automate-exploitation: Automated privilege escalation and SEO injection (execution)

PentestGPT automates privilege escalation, lateral movement; AI scripts generate SQL injection payloads adapting to WAF; inject SEO spam into CMS databases (backlinks to gambling, pharma, counterfeit sites); install webshells for persistence

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### monetization: SEO fraud and click fraud (impact)

Monetize via SEO spam affiliate schemes, click fraud; 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026; AI automation enables high-volume low-sophistication fraud operations

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### Connections

- cms-exploitation -> deploy-ai-tools
- deploy-ai-tools -> automate-exploitation
- automate-exploitation -> monetization

# FakeAgent Claude Desktop malvertising

- ID: huntress-fakeagent-claude-malvertising-2026-07
- Reported: 2026-07-22
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/huntress-fakeagent-claude-malvertising-2026-07/

## Summary
Huntress (Michael Tigges, 22 July 2026) calls this campaign FakeAgent. Bing ads for a Claude Desktop download pointed at a public Claude Artifact, claude.ai/public/artifacts/ca456f1f-44c0-42af-b329-4f1c7534a877, which had about 7,100 views and the platform disclaimer that the content is user-generated and unverified. Anthropic had removed the artifact by the time the post was published. The artifact redirected to claude.ai.download-app.us and then downloading-api.it.com/html/claude/win, which served a fake ClaudeDesktop.exe. download-app.us was registered on 9 May 2026. ClaudeDesktop.exe is a signed JetBrains jcef_helper.exe, the same file Huntress also saw copied as DockerDesktop.exe for a scheduled task. It sideloads a VMProtect-packed libcef.dll. That DLL reads an Ethereum contract, downloads cache.dat, and the task keeps a copy under the EdgeUpdate install directory. A second stage, sslconf.exe, is a signed IBM SPSS binary that sideloads tempdir.dll. That DLL checks the GPU vendor and VRAM, skips QEMU and VMware, and decrypts appcfg.dat with a DirectX shader used as an AES-256-CTR routine. The embedded payload is SectopRAT, an HVNC .NET RAT. Its C2 address is stored on a BNB Smart Chain contract. Huntress observed the campaign against 29 organizations on 21 and 22 July 2026. The live C2 in the post is 2.24.131.246, with backup domain 5ca8758c-02d0-4a72-89c8-d468b66dda41.com.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Unnamed. Huntress ties the download domain to one registrant who also held earlier domains, including one Microsoft seized, and an April 2026 fake Docker Desktop that used the same sideload. No person or group is named.

- Actor: Unnamed
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: cybercrime
- Attributed by: Huntress (Michael Tigges)
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Bing ads for a Claude Desktop download, leading to a public Claude Artifact and then a fake Windows installer.
- Victims and sectors: 29 organizations. Huntress does not name them or their sectors.
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: Huntress does not name a victim country. The registrant's location is not a victim region and is not recorded here.
- Scale and metrics: 29 organizations, 21-22 July 2026. The artifact had about 7,100 views before Anthropic removed it.

## Attack flow
### ad: Bing ad opens an artifact (access)

An ad for a Claude Desktop download sends the visitor to a public Claude Artifact. The page is user-generated. Anthropic later removed it.

Evidence: <https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat>

### redirect: Artifact redirects to the installer (ai)

The artifact sends the browser to claude.ai.download-app.us and then to downloading-api.it.com, which serves the fake ClaudeDesktop.exe.

Evidence: <https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat>

### sideload: Signed host loads libcef.dll (execution)

The signed JetBrains binary sideloads a VMProtect libcef.dll. A scheduled task keeps a DockerDesktop.exe copy, and a signed IBM binary later sideloads tempdir.dll.

Evidence: <https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat>

### rat: SectopRAT reads its C2 from chain (impact)

tempdir.dll decrypts appcfg.dat after a GPU check. The embedded SectopRAT reads its live C2, 2.24.131.246, from a BNB Smart Chain contract.

Evidence: <https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat>

### Connections

- ad -> redirect
- redirect -> sideload
- sideload -> rat

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0073](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0073) Impersonation — The ad, the public artifact, and the installer impersonate Claude Desktop.
  Evidence: <https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat>
- [AML.T0052](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0052) Phishing — Search ads deliver the fake installer. The lure is the AI product name, and the payload is not an email.
  Evidence: <https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat>

## Prevention
Download Claude Desktop from Anthropic. Treat a search ad and a public artifact as unverified. Alert when a signed JetBrains or IBM binary loads an unsigned DLL from the same directory, and when a new scheduled task runs DockerDesktop.exe from an EdgeUpdate path.

## Detections
- [Windows Unsigned DLL Side-Loading In Same Process Path](https://github.com/splunk/security_content/blob/develop/detections/endpoint/windows_unsigned_dll_side_loading_in_same_process_path.yml) (splunk) — Selected from a security-detections-mcp search for unsigned DLL side-loading. Sysmon Event 7 where an unsigned DLL loads from the same directory as the process, outside Windows and Program Files. That matches libcef.dll beside the signed JetBrains host and tempdir.dll beside the signed IBM host. A valid signature on the DLL would not match.
- [Scheduled Task Creation Via Schtasks.EXE](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_schtasks_creation.yml) (sigma) — Selected from a security-detections-mcp search for schtasks creation. Matches schtasks.exe with " /create " in the command line, excluding a system user. Huntress does not publish the command line. A task created through the Task Scheduler API would not match.
- [Local Scheduled Task Creation](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/windows/persistence_local_scheduled_task_creation.toml) (elastic) — Selected from a security-detections-mcp search for scheduled task creation. Requires an untrusted process or a listed script host, then schtasks.exe /create with a scheduling flag, within one minute, and not at SYSTEM integrity. The same command-line limit applies. Huntress did not show schtasks.exe.
- Sideload path and task location gaps (guidance) — Sigma Abusable DLL Potential Sideloading From Suspicious Location does list libcef.dll, but only under Perflogs, Users\Public, Temporary Internet Files, Windows\Temp, Favorites, Contacts, and Pictures. It does not cover a Downloads or AppData copy, so it is not cited. Sigma Scheduled Task Executed From A Suspicious Location matches Temp, Desktop, Downloads, and Public, not AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate. No Elastic image-load rule in the index covers a generic unsigned DLL beside a signed host.

## Source notes
Classified as adversary use of AI with the lure role, the same treatment as the Adception fake Claude installer and the ANY.RUN fake AI-tool installers. The AI product is the bait. Anthropic's platform hosted a user-generated artifact, and Huntress does not describe a compromise of Claude or of Anthropic. SectopRAT steals broadly. That is not recorded as a second role of AI-credential theft. Huntress used Claude Opus 4.8 while recovering a one-byte mistake in the shader key. That is the analyst's method, not the attacker's, and it is not an indicator. Benign signed hosts, which should not be blocked on the hash alone, are ClaudeDesktop.exe and DockerDesktop.exe SHA256 f8acb8f5cf88b77a4c27d7fd6856aa299bb178e85f9963c2fbd447d818da3ed0 (JetBrains jcef_helper.exe) and SSLConf.exe SHA256 fd826215add30c1319eefa291b6eaf8ddfa7720cfe816c49aef6fe8a88de7939 (IBM SPSS). Huntress quotes the second persistence path as %APPDATA%\Roaming\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\Install\sslconf.exe. The libcef.dll contract is 0xc1907d7be91f95903ad66d775c397302e7dd9228 and the SectopRAT contract is 0xe012d0f34cde9b870e9d9ed566ea5f8fd9b92228. polse.us is an earlier domain Huntress links to the same registrant. Microsoft seized it in Operation Endgame as StealC hosting. It is not a host of the July installer. An April 2026 Docker Hub fake Docker Desktop used the same libcef.dll sideload. The registrant email is omitted.

- deploy-agent -> autonomous-ops
- autonomous-ops -> encrypt
